newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sharp gold price fall would be temporary - West LB.
newsitem.headline: Sharp gold price fall would be temporary - West LB.

text.p: A sharp decline in gold bullion prices, should support of $336.40 be breached, would be overruled by bullish supply and demand fundamentals, WestLB bank said in a market report for investors.
"We don't see a sustained period below $320 an ounce," it said.
A significant number of mines with average production costs of $334 in South Africa and $358 in Australia was due to be closed, with the average world mining cost $317, the report said.
But mine production of 2,346 tonnes in 1996 already lagged jewellery demand alone of 2,807 tonnes, it argued.

The effects of this supply gap should counterbalance the bearish impact from the debate on the revaluation of German gold reserves in order to meet budgetary limits under European Monetary Union criteria.
